headline: Pricing-driven beat; guidance raised again
summary_short: FICO's fiscal Q3 2026 revenue rose to $674.2M (+25.7% y/y, -2.5% q/q) on Scores segment strength, with diluted EPS of $10.45 (+41.2% y/y); the company raised full-year FY2026 revenue, net income and EPS guidance.
summary_long: Revenue rose 25.7% y/y to $674.2M on Scores segment strength — B2B pricing (higher mortgage-origination unit price) drove a 49% B2B increase, while Software grew just 2% as ARR rose 10% y/y (platform +62%, non-platform -17%). Operating income grew 38.1% y/y to $362.6M; net income rose 30.5% y/y to $237.2M ($10.45 diluted EPS). FICO raised FY2026 revenue, net income and EPS guidance. Long-term debt rose to $5,582.4M (+100.8% y/y), funding $3,046.0M of nine-month buybacks and widening the shareholders' equity deficit to -$4,097.1M.

drivers.explanation: CEO Will Lansing attributed the quarter's strong results to "the successful execution of our strategic priorities" and used that to justify raising full-year guidance; no more specific operational cause was disclosed at the release level.

Scores revenue grew 41% y/y: B2B rose 49% on a higher mortgage-origination scores unit price, B2C rose 5% on higher indirect royalties via credit reporting agencies. Software grew a slower 2% as ARR rose 10% y/y (platform +62%, non-platform -17%). The q/q decline is not addressed in the release.

Tracks the revenue growth above; cost of revenue was roughly flat y/y (-0.6%), so gross-margin expansion follows mechanically from the revenue mix shift toward higher-margin Scores. Not separately discussed in the release.
Revenue growth (+25.7% y/y) outpaced R&D (+13.8% y/y) and SG&A (+22.8% y/y) growth; the release does not explain the SG&A increase specifically.
Not a line the release labels separately; tracks the operating-income growth described above.
Not a labeled release metric; adds back depreciation and amortization ($12.1M for the nine months per the cash-flow statement, not broken out quarterly) to operating income.
Tracks pretax income growth; effective tax rate rose to 24.6% from 23.3% a year ago, a modest offset to income growth. The release does not itemize the tax-rate change.
Tracks net income growth, amplified by a lower diluted share count (22.703M vs 24.575M a year ago) from ongoing buybacks.
Mirrors the diluted EPS move above; basic share count also fell y/y (22.670M vs 24.284M) on the same buyback activity.
Tracks operating-income growth, partly offset by higher other expense, net ($48.0M vs $25.5M a year ago); the release does not itemize the increase in other expense.

Cash rose despite $3,046.0M of nine-month buybacks, as nine-month operating cash flow ($777.9M) and $1.0B of new senior notes issued in the nine months more than offset repurchases and debt repayments; the release does not walk a quarterly cash bridge.

Debt roughly doubled y/y as the company issued $1.0B of new senior notes and drew on revolver/term loans over the nine months (partly offset by $400M of note repayments and $1,015.0M of revolver paydowns) to fund buybacks; not attributed to a specific driver beyond the cash-flow detail.
Current maturities on debt rose to $300.0M q/q from zero as a portion of long-term debt shifted into the current bucket; not separately explained in the release.

The deficit widened as $3,046.0M of nine-month share repurchases exceeded retained net income; FICO has carried negative equity for several years from sustained debt-funded buybacks, per the balance sheet.
Share count fell as nine-month buybacks ($3,046.0M) outpaced dilution from equity compensation; not separately explained beyond the cash-flow buyback figure.
